source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source_name: Mimosa aculeaticarpa Ortega var. biuncifera (Benth.) Barneby

morphology_source_reported.growth_habit: Rounded or somewhat spindly woody shrub, ca. 1 m tall
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Twice even-pinnately compound [genus]; 4–8 pairs of pinnae [key branch]
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Petals fused halfway or more; whitish filaments faintly pink [key branch]
morphology_source_reported.fruits: 35 mm long or shorter; mostly 3–4 mm broad and with marginal recurved prickles [key branch]
morphology_source_reported.diagnostic_characters: Armed shrub with frequently zigzag stems and conspicuous prickles on fruit margins

habitat_source_reported: Calcareous or sandy rocky openings, also alluvial soils
cautions: Repository name Mimosa biuncifera is historical synonym cited explicitly in Flora, which treats it as var. biuncifera under M. aculeaticarpa
